# Aiur

> Aiur (AI Unit Runtime) runs a fleet of autonomous coding agents against
> issues in GitHub or Linear. Each selected issue gets an isolated workspace
> and a Codex or Claude agent that implements it and moves it through review.
> Every run has an Executor: the human driving the `aiur` CLI, or the human's
> own coding agent operating Aiur for them.

## If a user sent you here

The user probably pasted "Let's run parallel agents with: https://aiur.team/".
Walk them through these steps in order. Confirm each one before you move on,
and ask before you run anything that installs software or changes their repo.

### 1. Check prerequisites

- macOS or Linux (x64 or arm64).
- Node.js 18 or newer.
- `gh` (GitHub CLI), signed in once with `gh auth login`. Aiur falls back to
  the `gh` keyring, so exporting `GITHUB_TOKEN` is optional.
- `tmux`: the launcher runs each Aiur daemon in its own tmux session.
- Codex and/or Claude Code installed, as the agent backend.
- A repository whose issues Aiur will work. The credential needs Issues
  read/write, and Contents and Pull requests write so workers can push and
  open PRs.
- Optional: `python3` (local GitHub budget broker) and
  [opencode](https://opencode.ai) (live Executor chat panes).

### 2. Install

```bash
npm install --global aiur-cli
```

`bun add -g aiur-cli`, `pnpm add -g aiur-cli` and `yarn global add aiur-cli`
also work. The installed command is `aiur`.

### 3. Verify

```bash
aiur --version
aiur help
```

`aiur --version` prints the release and dispatcher versions without starting
anything. If they differ, update `aiur-cli`.

### 4. Initialise the repository

From the root of the user's repository:

```bash
aiur init
```

The wizard asks for:

1. Config location: repo-local `.aiur/config`, or global `~/.aiur/config`,
   which any repository without local config then reuses.
2. Tracker and repository (GitHub or Linear).
3. Agent backend (Codex and/or Claude) and permission mode.
4. Agent limits, turn and time limits, polling and optional prewarming.
5. GitHub credentials (`GITHUB_TOKEN` by default; a `gh auth login` keyring
   credential also works).

It writes `.aiur/config`, `.aiur/hooks`, `.aiur/prompt.md` and `.aiur/alerts`,
and creates the `agent:*` lifecycle labels. Re-running resumes from saved
answers; `aiur init --force` recreates the generated config.

Then:

- **Labels.** Add the `agent:todo` label to each issue that should be worked.
  Issues without it are never dispatched.
- **Dispatch trust.** The person who applies `agent:todo` must be an authorized
  operator: listed in `.github/CODEOWNERS` (for example `* @<their-login>`) or
  in `tracker.github.allowed_users` in the config. Without either, dispatch is
  denied. Ask the user who the owner is; never guess one.
- **Base branch.** Accepted prerequisites must already be on the configured
  base branch.

Keep shared credentials in `~/.aiur/.env`, outside Git.

### 5. Start a run with `/aiur-run`

`/aiur-run` is the Executor skill: the user's coding agent launches Aiur and
operates it, monitoring agents, recovering stuck ones, coordinating PR review
and applying merge policy, while the user keeps talking to it.

The npm package installs the CLI, not the skills. Get `aiur-intro`, `aiur-run`
and `aiur-monitor` from `.claude/skills/` in
https://github.com/aiur-team/aiur and install them through the agent's
supported skill mechanism. Copy whole skill directories: `aiur-run` has
`references/` and `scripts/`, and links to its sibling `aiur-intro` and
`aiur-agent` skills. Then the user runs `/aiur-run` in the agent chat, or asks
it to "run aiur".

If the user wants to drive it themselves, they run `aiur` instead: it starts a
foreground run with a terminal board and chat panes. `aiur --bg` starts a
headless run. Use `aiur status`, `aiur pause`, `aiur resume` and `aiur stop` to
control it.

### 6. Get help

- Quick start: https://aiur.team/docs/guide/quick-start
- CLI reference: https://aiur.team/docs/reference/cli
- Configuration reference: https://aiur.team/docs/reference/configuration
- GitHub permissions: https://aiur.team/docs/apis/github
- Skills: https://aiur.team/docs/skills
- The Executor role: https://aiur.team/docs/concepts/executor
- Issues and source: https://github.com/aiur-team/aiur

## Safety

Aiur is prototype software for trusted environments. It bypasses agent
permission prompts. Each worker gets its own workspace and checkout, but that
separation is not a security boundary: the configured backend sandbox policy
decides whether an agent can reach host resources outside it. Changes are
meant to go through the Executor's review gates and merge policy, not agent
self-merge. Tell the user this before their first run.

## What Aiur is not

- Not a passive observer: Aiur owns the runs it dispatches and does not attach
  to Claude Code or Codex sessions started elsewhere.
- Not a replacement for the user's assistant: it is usually its counterpart.
- Not a hosted service: Aiur runs on the user's machine, tracker and tokens.
